Hi Sophie — thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap and the specific asks we promised to follow up on.

Call summary (short):
- Primary use case: real-time classification + streaming summarization for clinician notes.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~400 QPS across the product (global), with up to 2,000 QPS burst for peak events.
- Concurrency per user/session: typically 4–8 heavy concurrent streams.
- Streaming requirement: sub-200ms incremental response delivery for live transcription chunks; finalization latency target lower (p95 goal below 1s for commit tokens).
- Data residency: EU patient data must remain in EU region; APAC pilot customers require in-region processing (data residency + at-rest storage).

Performance targets we discussed (initial targets, engineering to confirm):
- US (primary region): inference p95 latency target 50–120ms per token (depends on model size); end-to-end request p95 target 150–300ms.
- EU: inference p95 latency target 70–160ms; end-to-end ~200–350ms.
- APAC: inference p95 latency target 120–250ms; end-to-end ~300–500ms (depends on nearest region availability).

Edge behaviors / routing notes:
- We recommend regional routing by customer tenancy + geo-fallback to nearest compatible model variant when in-region capacity is constrained.
- For strict residency tenants we will pin requests to the EU or APAC cluster (no cross-border routing).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you share a representative traffic sample (small JSONL of 200 requests) and the expected peak QPS per region? (attached example file name: finexa-test-traffic.jsonl)
2) Please confirm which domains/customers must be forced to EU-only processing (list of tenant IDs or domain names).
3) Will you need persistent storage of transcripts in-region, or is ephemeral processing sufficient?
4) Schedule: propose a 60-min technical deep-dive where Marissa (solutions eng) and Ben (SRE) join to map exact SLOs and testing plan. My availability: Tue/Wed next week 10–12 PT and Thu 14–16 PT.

Attachments: finexa-performance-matrix.xlsx (initial SLO/throughput matrix), network-topology-diagram.png

Thanks,

Sophie — answering the technical bits you called out. Quoting your question: 

> "is that per chunk emission or per token? Our requirement is that clinicians see partial updates within 250ms of audio arrival for 250ms audio frames."

Short answer: we target chunk emission latency (end-to-end) rather than per-token micro-latency. For audio frames of 250ms we can pipeline chunked encoding -> model streaming with a target p95 chunk emission below 250ms in-region, assuming network RTT is within region. If your audio ingest point is outside the region the effective latency will be higher.

Model placement and caching:
- Recommended approach for your workload: per-region replica sets (EU/US/APAC) for pinned tenants to maximize KV cache locality (conversation state + prefix caches). This improves cache hit rates and reduces cost for conversational re-use.
- We can offer a multi-region pool with intelligent routing for non-residency tenants; however cache locality will be lower and you will see ~10–25% higher token compute due to cache misses (depends on session affinity).

Networking / security notes: 
- Ingestion options: public API with IP allowlist, or direct VPC peering / PrivateLink for lowest RTT. We recommend VPC peering for production pilot.
- Encryption: TLS1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest. For EU-regulated tenants we can integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM for at-rest keys.
- Data retention: by default we offer ephemeral KV cache (not persisted); if you require stored transcripts we will place them in region-bound object storage and enforce access controls.

Failover behavior:
- For pinned (residency) tenants we do NO cross-border failover unless explicitly enabled. For others we implement prioritized routing: primary region -> neighboring region -> global fallback. We expose policies to configure per-tenant.

Testing & pilot details:
- Suggested pilot: 2 weeks with a sandbox set of tenants; we capture p50/p95/p99 for chunk emission, end-to-end request latency, error rate, and throughput.
- Test harness: use the attached finexa-test-traffic.jsonl (sample schema) and run 3 traffic profiles (steady, spike, churn). We will provide a JMeter/Locust template if you prefer.

I've uploaded a short runbook and suggested SLO matrix here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_finexa-perf
